questions.text: Give a comparative discussion about alphabet, language, and power of alphabet.

Design a Deterministic Finite Automata (DFA) that accepts the language L such that $L=\{w \mid w \text{ starts with 0 and has odd length or starts with 1 and has even length}\}$. How will you test the membership of a string using the above DFA?
What is the basic difference between the extended transition functions of DFA and Nondeterministic Finite Automata (NFA)? Explain with an example.
How can you verify whether a regular language is empty or not.

Write regular expression/definition for the following languages:

- (i) All strings containing no more than two $a$'s over alphabet $\{a, b, c\}$.
- (ii) The set of strings of $0$'s and $1$'s whose number of $1$'s is divisible by four and whose number of $0$'s is even.
- (iii) All string of digits with at most one repeated digit.
- (iv) All Strings which contain no run's of $a$'s of length greater than two over alphabet $\{a, b, c\}$.

Design a NFA that accepts set of all strings of $a$'s and $b$'s such that there are two $a$'s separated by a number of positions that is divisible by 3. Also show the states NFA will be in during the processing of valid input.

questions.text: Construct an $\varepsilon$-NFA equivalent to $(0+1)^*(0+11)$.
Prove that if $L=L(A)$ for some DFA A, then there is a regular expression R such that $L=L(R)$.

Consider the following grammar:

$$\begin{aligned}
S &\to AB \mid AS \\
A &\to aA \mid \varepsilon \\
B &\to BB \mid AB \mid bb
\end{aligned}$$

Answer these questions

- (i) What's shortest string it accepts? Are there more than one that length?
- (ii) What language does it generate?
- (iii) Show this grammar is ambiguous.
Give a context Free Grammar (CFG) for the language of balanced parenthesis and squared brackets. How would you interpret the string "([[()[]]([])]())"?

questions.text: Define CFG. Construct a CFG for the given expression: $(a+b)(a+b+0+1)^*$
What is push down automata (PDA)? How does it differ from $\varepsilon$-NFA?
Construct deterministic PDA to accept the following language, $L=\{0^n1^n \mid n>0\}$.
Prove the theorem, let L be $L(P_F)$ for some PDA $P_F$ where $P_F=(Q,\Sigma,\Gamma,\delta_F,q_0,z_0,F)$ then there is a PDA $P_N$ such that $L = N(P_N)$.
Why is it that the transition function for DPDA's only works for 1 alphabet symbol and 1 stack symbol?

Consider the following grammar

$$\begin{aligned}
S &\to AACD \\
A &\to aAb \mid \varepsilon \\
C &\to aC \mid a \\
D &\to aDa \mid bDb \mid \varepsilon
\end{aligned}$$

And simply safe order

- (i) Eliminate $\varepsilon$-production.
- (ii) Eliminate unit production.
- (iii) Eliminate Useless symbols
- (iv) Put the grammar in CNF
Discuss about PDA acceptance (i) From empty stack to final state and (ii) From final state to empty stack.
State pumping lemma for CFL's and its advantages
Use pumping lemma to show the following (i) $a^nb^mc^p$ is context free for $n \ge 0$, $m \ge 0$ and $p=n$. (ii) $a^nb^mc^p$ is not context free for $n \ge 0$, $m=2n$ and $p=m+n$.

Convert the following grammar to a PDA that accepts the same language by empty stack.

$$\begin{aligned}
S &\to 0S1 \mid A \\
S &\to 1A0 \mid S \mid \varepsilon
\end{aligned}$$
